Subject: High 500 rate + queueing on our reserved pool (FinAI - urgent)

David —

We started seeing a sustained spike in 500 responses and timeouts hitting our reserved pool around 08:45 PT this morning. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to ~6% and p95 latency jumped from 320ms to ~3.4s. We're also seeing long token queueing (requests waiting > 1.5s before being scheduled). Sample request IDs attached and a short error log (finai-error-snapshot-20270607.log).

This is on our Dedicated reservation (region: us-west-2, model: rwd-3b-quant) — traffic profile hasn't changed on our side; no increased QPS. Our engineers saw KV cache mismatches causing repeated context warmups. Impact: critical features in production are returning 500s for customers on VIP plan.

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity saturation or a runtime anomaly? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can route our traffic to a fallback variant while this is resolved. Procurement is also asking whether this triggers SLA credits — copying them.

Attaching: finai-error-snapshot-20270607.log

Thanks,
Alex Ops
Platform Ops — FinAI

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 500 rate + queueing on our reserved pool (FinAI - urgent)

Quick triage notes from SRE side after looking at live metrics:
- Dedicated pool finai-dedicated-usw2-07 shows sustained GPU memory pressure with long tail GC / allocation delays from 08:44–09:05 PT. CUDA SM usage maxed and queue depth increased (attached heatmap: finai-sla-usage-heatmap.png).
- Correlation: a handful (~0.6% of requests) with >12k token contexts came in during a 5-minute burst — these dominate memory churn and KV cache misses.
- Runtime kernels: no recent rollout flags on the cluster, but we are seeing fallback to slower attention path for large sequences which increases per-token time.

Mitigation plan (immediate):
1) Apply per-customer request-size throttle and reject >8k token requests with 413 to prevent churn (SRE, now).
2) Route new VIP requests to rwd-3b-int8-fallback in a gradual fashion (routing team, 10–15 min).
3) Temporarily add 2 spare nodes to the dedicated pool (capacity ops) — requires low-latency placement, ETA 25–40 min.
4) Runtime to enable KV cache sticky policy for FinAI to avoid repeated warmups (jonas).

I'll push logs to the bridge and attach the heatmap. If we see immediate improvement after routing, we'll keep the fallback until a safer kernel path is validated.

— Soojin
SRE, Redwood Inference

Quick exec summary after remediation actions:

- Short-term mitigations executed: request-size throttle, fallback routing, capacity add, KV policy.
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden burst of long-context requests caused KV cache churn and pushed the Dedicated pool into allocation stalls; no single kernel regression identified — we are running a postmortem.

- Exec POC: David Kim (you have my direct number) and Marissa Cole. If you want an org-level bridge at C-level, we can schedule immediately.
